title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is part of a plan for a 'surgery' theory of conformal surfaces: (1) Thm 2: compact conformal surfaces with boundary are equivalent to proper smooth real algebraic curves; (2) cutting a conformal surface X along a topological 1-complex K; (3) regluing. Theorem 3 (previous page) says that the cut surface X~, with the sheaf of continuous functions that are holomorphic on Int(X~) = X \ K, is a conformal surface with boundary. The page proves this locally. It must produce, at every boundary point of X~, a chart to the half-disc H ∩ D° (H the closed upper half-plane, D° the open unit disc) that is holomorphic in the interior. The page opens by splitting into two cases: a point of K of order >= 2, or of order 1 (an endpoint).

Lemma 2. Let K ⊂ C be a finite union of topological segments. There is a hesitant, parenthetical regularity hypothesis: rectifiable? smooth??. Let x ∈ K.

(a) Suppose x is not an endpoint of K. Then there is a continuous injective map f : H ∩ D° → C, holomorphic on (Int H) ∩ D°, with f(]-1,1[) ⊂ K and f(0) = x. Moreover, for a prescribed bank ('rive') of K at x, one may assume the image f(H ∩ D°) is a one-sided neighbourhood of x lying on that bank.

(b) Suppose x is an endpoint of K. Then there is f : H ∩ D° → C, holomorphic in the interior, with f(0) = x. Completed on the next page: f is injective on the open half-disc with image in C \ K. The restrictions f|]-1,0] and f|[0,1[ are each injective and have the same image in K. So the diameter folds onto the end of the slit, which is the model sqrt(z - x) chart at the tip of a slit.

In modern terms this is the local boundary-correspondence (Carathéodory / prime-end) theory for slit and Jordan-arc boundaries. One takes a small Jordan or slit domain bounded by part of K and a crosscut and applies the Riemann map. Carathéodory's theorem shows the map extends continuously, homeomorphically off the slit. At an endpoint, each interior point of the slit corresponds to two prime ends. The lemma gives exactly the charts that make X~ a bordered Riemann surface; it is the 'cutting' step of the surgery.

The next page draws the key consequence (Scholie). Each bank induces on K a canonical real-analytic structure, via the boundary charts. The identity map between the two structures is in general not real-analytic, and these induced regularity properties do not reflect the regularity of K in C. This is precisely the phenomenon of conformal welding: the welding homeomorphism of an arc or curve.
errors: The regularity hypothesis Grothendieck hesitates over (rectifiable? smooth?) is unnecessary. By Carathéodory's theorem on Jordan domains and the prime-end theory for slits, the lemma holds for arbitrary topological arcs, which Grothendieck seems to suspect with his '??'.

As stated, (a) speaks of 'x not an endpoint' but K is a union of segments. At a branch point of order >= 3 there are several sectors, and ]-1,0] and [0,1[ map onto two different arcs of K. The 'for a given bank' clause covers this only if 'bank' is read as 'sector'.
The requirement that f(H ∩ D°) be a relatively open neighbourhood of x in (bank ∪ K) is implicit rather than stated. Without it the map would not give a chart.
In (b) the condition reads f(0)=0 (or is ambiguous); it should be f(0)=x, as corrected on the next page.

ideas.what: Local boundary charts of a domain slit along a topological arc: two-sided charts at interior points of the arc, and a folded (square-root type) chart at an endpoint.
ideas.modern_name: Carathéodory boundary correspondence / prime ends for slit domains

ideas.what: Cutting a Riemann surface along a 1-complex yields a bordered Riemann surface (Theorem 3).
ideas.modern_name: Bordered Riemann surfaces obtained by cutting; Ahlfors–Sario style surgery
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in the general program of Esquisse d'un programme (1984) on conformal/topological surgery; unsure

ideas.what: Compact bordered conformal surfaces are equivalent to smooth proper real algebraic curves (Thm 2, previous page).
Each bank of an arc induces a real-analytic structure on it, and the two are related by a non-analytic homeomorphism (Scholie, next page).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical local lemma (Carathéodory boundary correspondence for slit domains), serving Grothendieck's programme of conformal surgery. The neighbouring Scholie rediscovers the conformal-welding phenomenon, which is well established in the literature. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line under 'Lemme 2': the parenthetical reads roughly '(On suppose K sans singularités (rectifiable?), lisse???)' and is circled as a tentative hypothesis.
In (b), 'f(0) = 0' is likely 'f(0) = x' (or an uncorrected slip); the next page states f(0)=x.
In (b), the final crossed-out lines read approximately 'soit ... f|]-1,0] et f|[0,1[ soient injectives'. That condition is moved, uncrossed, to the next page as condition c).

In (a), 'telle h.l.' among the struck lines is probably the start of a struck-out phrase before 'application continue injective'; the surviving sense is 'il existe une application continue injective f : H ∩ D° → C, holomorphe dans (Int H) ∩ D°'.
